title: Where the work runs
caption: Choose the layer from evidence: faster kernels cannot remove an exposed host or network wait.

title: Compute and bandwidth ceilings
caption: Schematic roofline: changing shape or reuse moves a workload; peak rates do not establish achieved performance.

title: Active work and resident experts
caption: A token activates selected experts; unused experts can still occupy memory or require sharded placement.

title: Submission is not completion
caption: Host submission timing can end while GPU work is still running. Synchronize at the boundary appropriate to the question.

title: Feed the device without losing ownership
caption: Pipeline throughput is limited by the slowest stage; pinning or asynchronous APIs alone do not guarantee overlap.

title: Saved values connect forward and backward
caption: Backward needs the declared saved state. Fusion, views and in-place changes must preserve the autograd contract.

title: Compilation chooses execution paths
caption: Generated kernels and library calls are alternative implementation choices. Shape guards and graph breaks affect the cost.

title: Grid, blocks and storage scopes
caption: A block owns shared memory; registers belong to threads. Cross-block synchronization needs an explicit valid mechanism.

title: A reduction is a dependency tree
caption: Parallel order changes rounding. Masks, synchronization and participation rules remain part of correctness.

title: Reuse tiles before returning to HBM
caption: The highlighted K slice contributes to one output tile. Reuse improves intensity but consumes registers and shared memory.

title: Overlap movement and matrix work
caption: The next tile must be ready before consumption, and a buffer cannot be overwritten while compute still reads it.

title: Stream K/V and retain online row state
caption: Running maximum, denominator and weighted sum are rescaled together; dense attention arithmetic remains quadratic.

title: A faster matrix stage can expose softmax
caption: Hardware co-design balances movement, matrix operations and non-matmul work. Diagram lengths are conceptual.

title: Packing saves bytes; scales consume some
caption: For 1,024 weights, group size 32 and FP32 scales, int4 uses 512 + 128 = 640 array bytes before headers and alignment.

title: Different precision paths need different evidence
caption: AMP, training recipes and post-training quantization operate at different points. Conversion alone does not prove quality or speed.

title: Shards become transient full parameters
caption: Persistent sharding reduces one budget; gathered layers, activations and prefetch buffers still contribute to peak memory.

title: Collective semantics and physical traffic
caption: Reduce-scatter followed by all-gather produces an all-reduce result; the library can select another physical algorithm.

title: A concrete eight-rank layout
caption: DP=2, TP=2, PP=2, CP=1 gives eight ranks. This drawing does not establish expert-group legality or physical placement.

title: Trace the decision through code boundaries
caption: Pin source revisions, follow inputs and constraints, then distinguish a documented path from an observed runtime dispatch.

title: The hottest expert can determine the tail
caption: Both cases contain 34 assignments. Skew changes expert shapes and balance, even though the average assignment count is unchanged.

title: Recover the same training trajectory
caption: The local CPU lab checks losses, parameters and optimizer tensors; omitting RNG restoration is a deliberate failing control.

title: One cancellation must preserve the other owner
caption: Logical sequences can share compatible prefix blocks. References and in-flight work determine when storage is reclaimable.

title: A matching suffix is not a matching history
caption: Identity includes the compatible computation and allowed sharing domain. A semantic answer cache has a different validity rule.

title: Bound interruptions to existing decode
caption: A smaller prefill chunk creates more decode opportunities but can add overhead and postpone prompt completion. Bars are schematic.

title: Compare the same total resources
caption: Two colocated workers and one prefill plus one decode worker each use two devices. State movement and queueing can change the result.

title: Verify the draft before keeping its state
caption: Keep the accepted prefix; correct the first rejected token and discard later speculative state. The lab validates one categorical step.

title: State has a lifetime while the agent waits
caption: Compare resume work and displaced capacity across a complete task; idle byte-seconds alone do not select a policy.

title: The producer and loader meet at an artifact
caption: Record input, target and runtime contracts. Exported graph archives and compiled packages can share a suffix but need different loaders.

title: Delegation does not remove boundary costs
caption: Count conversion, transfer and fallback between graph partitions. The validated lab uses one unquantized CPU XNNPACK segment.

title: CPU, scale-up and scale-out are different paths
caption: Conceptual traffic boundaries, not a complete board/rack layout. Local HBM, coherent links and network transfers have different costs.

title: A 2× component improvement becomes 1.43× overall
caption: Constructed disjoint phase example: 60 s compute + 40 s other becomes 30 + 40 = 70 s for the same useful work.

title: The claim must survive every evidence gate
caption: Keep raw outcomes, adverse cases and rejected candidates. A well-supported rejection is a useful engineering result.

title: Choose an implementation, then validate it
caption: Libraries, graph compilation and custom kernels are alternative or composable paths; the target and numerical contract decide eligibility.

after: Layers: graph compilers, kernel DSLs, vendor targets
title: Graph compilers, kernel DSLs and vendor targets
caption: Arrows show kernel-DSL paths only; graph compilers also call vendor libraries and emit their own code. Dashed: an opaque custom call.

after: Lowering: a model becomes an artifact
title: Partition, then library or generated kernels
caption: Anchor operators usually reach a library or BYOC code generator; the remaining operators are generated. Both end in one runtime artifact.
